name: Hollow Creek
blurb: A sleepy river town on Halloween night. Mystery Club HQ is at the south end of Main Street.

events.name: Blood Moon
events.blurb: A red moon rises. The Haunter's ectoplasm refills faster and every scare hits harder.

events.name: Thunderstorm
events.blurb: Lightning lights up the house for a heartbeat. Lamps flicker and sometimes blow out.

events.name: Pea-Soup Fog
events.blurb: A thick fog rolls in off the creek. You can barely see the end of your flashlight beam.

events.name: Power Outage
events.blurb: The whole street goes dark. Every lamp in the house starts off; flashlights drain faster.

events.name: Harvest Festival
events.blurb: The town is out celebrating. Solvers are braver (less fear), but dawn comes sooner.

rumours: Trick or treat! ... Are you the Mystery Club? My mum says you're real detectives!
The Historical Society might close after Halloween. Hardly anyone visits the museum.
Miss Wren at the museum gives out the best candy. Full-size bars!
My big brother saw a light up at the old windmill. Nobody's lived there for years.
Somebody borrowed the old festival masks from the museum. Grown-ups keep whispering about it.
If you go past the church, the bells ring by themselves at midnight. Probably.
The lighthouse on Gull Point is still lit. Nobody knows who keeps it going.

folk.pieceBlurb: the Mayor's old festival sash, cut down to size
folk.name: Mayor Harold Beaumont
folk.ask: Our prize pumpkin rolled clean off the festival cart and away down Elm Street, west of Main! Find it and the Mayor owes you one.
folk.thanks: The prize pumpkin! Splendid. I'll have a word with a few people for you.
lines: Lending the old masks to the festival was my idea. It seemed like a good idea at the time.
The museum's budget? Let's just say the board has been talking to a man from the city.
Hollow Creek has never been so well looked after. Don't tell the sheriff I said so.

folk.pieceBlurb: a tin moon on a string. 'For courage, dearie.'
folk.name: Old Nell Thistle
folk.ask: My cat Midnight has wandered off among the headstones behind the church. She likes the candles. Bring her home, dearie.
folk.thanks: Midnight! There you are. The cards say someone is lying about where they were tonight.
lines: The masks remember everyone who ever wore them. That's why they work.
I read the cards for a man in a fine waistcoat last week. Coins, coins, coins. And a key.
The oldest mask has no face of its own. It borrows yours.

folk.pieceBlurb: the Sunday-school handbell: ring it and the dark feels smaller
folk.name: Reverend Amos Gale
folk.ask: The sexton's lantern has gone from the churchyard gate. Someone saw it down by the bridge. We can't leave the dead in the dark tonight.
folk.thanks: Bless you. People tell a minister things. Ask one more of them where they really were.
lines: The founders carved the Hollow Creek Mask their first winter here, to frighten off whatever walked the woods.
Every mask in the museum was blessed in this church once. I'm not sure it took.
Edie Wren rings our bells on Sundays. There's ink on the bell rope every time.

folk.pieceBlurb: a coffee can with star holes punched in it and a candle inside
folk.name: Dot Kowalski
folk.ask: The wind took my door wreath clean off! Last I saw it was cartwheeling past the Post Office. Coffee's on me if you find it.
folk.thanks: My wreath! Here's a tip with your coffee: folks talk in my back booth, and I'll vouch for you.
lines: Busy night! Half the town's been in asking about those masks.
Mortimer Vane tips like it hurts him. Sat in my back booth with a fella from the city last week.
Rosa from the museum tea room buys my pie crusts. Don't tell a soul.

folk.pieceBlurb: a deputy's tin star, 'for the duration of the night'
folk.name: Sheriff Ruth Calloway
folk.ask: Some joker swiped the jack-o'-lantern off the station steps. Kids saw it heading for the Fire Station. Fetch it back? I'm on bridge duty.
folk.thanks: Much obliged. I'll tell folks to answer your questions straight.
lines: Nobody crosses this bridge after ten unless I wave them through. Quiet night so far.
Walter Finch and I go back. Thirty years walking that museum and never missed a night.
Plenty of folks heading out to Ravensford tonight. The train's running late again.

lots.name: Pemberton Cottage
lots.blurb: A tidy little cottage with a white picket fence. Mrs. Pemberton swears her teapot rattles at midnight. Small and quick: one floor, a garden and a shed.

lots.name: Hollow Creek Farm
lots.blurb: The Hatchers' farm at the edge of town. Lanterns float through the corn maze and something lives in the hayloft. Medium: a two-storey farmhouse, a barn and a big maze.

lots.name: Willow Lane Victorian
lots.blurb: The Ashcombe house: turrets, gingerbread trim and a music box that plays by itself in the nursery. Large: two floors and a tower, a gazebo and a family plot.

lots.name: Historical Society
lots.blurb: The Hollow Creek Historical Society: a red-brick museum with white columns, a gallery of folklore masks, a reading room that smells of lavender and old paper, and an archive upstairs. It may close after Halloween. Large: two floors, a courtyard and a workshop.

lots.name: Blackwood Manor
lots.blurb: The old Blackwood estate past the creek: a cellar, two floors and a roof, a greenhouse, a cemetery and a pumpkin patch. Huge: the longest night.
